answer: Each identity seals a unique 4 GB replica with a memory-hard encoding keyed to its public key, about 20 GPU minutes per seal, and commits the Merkle root on chain. Every epoch a beacon demands five random openings within 3 seconds, and a miss burns a 25 token bond. Cloning 10,000 identities needs 40 TB of disk, roughly 3,300 GPU hours, and 250,000 tokens at risk, near $4,500 before any reward. The fable of free identities ends here; each replica is a lantern that only shines over a real oasis of disk, and a fake leaves a dry well that peers can detect in one epoch.
